angleRead.name: Carmen Delaine
angleRead.text: The Fund has moved $6.6 million and the public record names two households. That's the story I've been tracking since the closeout order landed in C115. Now the charter renewal sits on the Council calendar for C117, and the mayor's gavel keeps saying the same thing: no final action until the C114 closeout is verified, business-and-resident scope intact, 23-day standard intact. What does not line up for me is the gap between the money that's moved and the accounting that's supposed to follow it. The tracker says $20.6 million remains of the $28 million. The last disbursement was C116. But the closeout publication that's supposed to verify where that $6.6 million went — that's still the thing

plan.focus: Whether the C114 closeout publication, when verified, actually meets the business-and-resident scope and 23-day standard that the Council made conditions of charter renewal — and what the $6.6 million in disbursements to date shows about who the Fund has actually reached.
plan.why: The Fund is the largest active economic initiative in West Oakland at $28 million, it passed 6-3 in C78, and the Council has now twice ordered closeout verification before renewal. The public record names two households but the tracker shows $6.6 million moved. That gap between named recipients and total disbursed is the civic-ledger question that matters: either the closeout accounts for the rest, or it doesn't, and either way the Council's 23-day standard gives me a concrete measure to hold th
checks: Pull the C114 closeout publication from the Council Clerk's record and check whether it itemizes disbursements by household and business, or aggregates in a way that hides the breakdown.
Compare the closeout's stated timeline against the 23-day standard the Council preserved in C115 and C116 — does the publication document dates that meet it, or does it fudge the clock?

Cross-reference the two named households in the public record against the closeout's total to see what percentage of the $6.6 million they represent, and whether the remainder is accounted for or simply absent.
Check whether the business-and-resident scope language in the closeout matches the scope language in the C115 and C116 milestones, or whether it narrows who qualifies.
Review the C116 disbursement entry against the closeout to see if the most recent money moved before or after the verification was supposed to be published.

unverifiedLead: The possibility that the closeout publication, when it appears, accounts for the $6.6 million through aggregated categories rather than named recipients, which would make the two named households a partial picture rather than the whole one.

The possibility that the 23-day standard in the closeout is measured from a different starting point than the Council's C115 order, which would make the verification technically compliant but substantively short.

The possibility that the remaining $20.6 million is the real story — that the disbursement pace slows or accelerates depending on what the closeout reveals, and that the charter renewal vote in C117 is where that pace gets set.
